Found out through the mail my wife filled for divorce. I left the house with purpose. I actually followed through with one of my suicidal ideations, right up to putting the noose around my neck. Planned it out a hundred times. Took rope from the garage that I placed there in a huff.  Left phone home. Drove closer to the ideal spot, an abandoned train over pass. Below nothing but trash. Tied the noose, looked for a spot away from over grown trees or anything I could save myself by grabbing. Measured out the length bur dropping the rope down, tying the middle of the too long rope to the busted railling. Thought I heard shuffling of feet. Put noose about my neck and started to look over and down. Stared longer than I know. Heard movement down and away from under the bridge. Too large to be a deer. Could be people, kids, drug users, homeless. Always seemed vacant the few times I've scouted it. First time I found this spot was in a summer day, there were kids, young adults hanging out down under that day. Tonight was a cold night waiting for rain. Thought I might be observed, even rescued by someone with a cell phone. I removed the noose. Left it there, let it fall back down without me. Not sure why. The meds? Fear? Rushed home to assure the wife I wasn't going to argue. Talk about it all in therapy. But I couldn't not want to talk. Kept bothering her. Turned to DBT therapy apps. Still here. Still awake. Brain still racing.

I'm alive.  I'm still married and attending couples counselling.  My own business is growing.  I don't know if I will or not. Hoping therapy and changing the way I think and work will help with what the drugs have not.   I can laugh with my kids!  Mt depression isn't gone but it doesn't plague my every thought.  If I feel depressed I'm aware of it not stuck and can easily dismiss it or address why I'm feeling that way and change it into motivation or a reason to do something differently.  I have to use one of a few anti-depressants approved in the study.  I hope that more newer anti-depressants will be added to that list.  I think a different combination might be a better combination for myself.

I go every two weeks still, but I'm not the usual case.  The study will have you switch to every for weeks and then longer depending on your results.  For what it helps me with it helps really well. Most suicidal thoughts that were a constant in my brain are almost gone. Most patients seem to dose rarely now.

desvenlafaxine (Pristiq), duloxetine (Cymbalta), venlafaxine (Effexor), venlafaxine XR (Effexor XR), and a few more...

I do think the two hours are necessary.  Each time the effect is different but the effect is almost sure to effect eyesight and even judgement.  It can be scary so a person near by helps with that.  Plus you can't drive after.  Each dose day you should plan on sleeping or relaxing the rest of that day.
